sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016. Change Request 2016-037 (create [xdo] Kwandu; adopted 2017-01-31): request form and new-code-element form, submitted by Linda Jordan with Sebastian Floor.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Names (xoKwandu, autonym Olukwandu, alt. Kwando), location (E13.11922 S13.80147), ~6,000 speakers, closest to Kuvale [olu] and Nyaneka [nyk], one segmental remark (alveolar laminal consonants as in Kuvale), a written Philemon and an oral Bible project. Published sources cited: Medeiros 1981 and 1984 only (ethnography, customary law).

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda. 2015. A Comparison of Five Speech Varieties of Southwestern Angola: Comparing OluHumbe, OluCilenge, OluKwandu, OluNgendelengo, and OluKuvale in the Kamucuio Municipality, Namibe Province. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-017. Dallas: SIL International. iii+29 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only linguistic source Glottolog lists for kwan1289: lexicostatistics, noun-class prefixes, segmental sound correspondences (sec. 4.3, table 5) and a 600-item OluKwandu wordlist with no prosodic marks. Sec. 4.3, p. 7: 'Tone is not covered in this paper in order to focus on the segmental correspondences.' Phonetic remarks on OluKwandu are segmental only (alveolar laminal consonants shared with Herero varieties; high frequency of palatal lateral in roots, pp. 8, 10-11). No word 'stress' or 'accent' occurs in the text.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (no. 93 'Ndombe or Kwando, 93a Koroka', Mossamedes coast; pp. 779-780, 800-801)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. The speech 'spoken by the Andombe, Akwando, and Akoroka tribes.. is as yet scarcely illustrated'; 8 words from W. J. B. Chapman (p. 780). Whether Johnston's coastal 'Kwando' is the Serra das Neves Kwandu [xdo] is uncertain (the ndom1244 check reads it as a Kwando/Kwisi label near Kuvale territory).
